core_obligations: Embed the finite configuration into a thin Delone set preserving existing hefty simplices.
Show every added covering simplex is already original when the query point lies in the k-hull, using deletion and Delaunay uniqueness.
Construct an added apex and auxiliary points giving strict deficiency outside the k-hull.
proof_roadmap: Thin Delone completion yields upper bounds
Inside the k-hull: deletion and Delaunay uniqueness yield equality
Outside the k-hull: explicit pyramid construction forces strict inequality
difficulty_reason: The inequality uses the global covering theorem as support, but the counted result adds a nontrivial exact equality criterion. Both directions require geometric constructions: identifying original simplices through deleted-point Delaunay triangulations, and constructing an exterior pyramid while preserving existing circumcircle emptiness data. This is more than a direct specialization of the infinite-set result.
